clue.text: During ceremony, legs beginning to tremble, given a small token

indicators.note: the other pieces sit during, that is inside, the word for ceremony

parts.note: pomp is stately ceremony
legs of a journey or race are stages

indicators.note: the beginning of the word tremble supplies its first letter only

explanation.surface: At a ceremony, someone with shaky legs is handed a small keepsake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a' reads as surface but supplies the letter A; 'During' splits the ceremony word after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp stuck on a letter is a small paper token showing the fee has been paid.

clue.text: Person turned back on then feels excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so the word feels is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who was rejected nonetheless feels a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: ON is taken as written and followed by ESELF, the rearrangement signalled by 'excited'; 'turned back' plays no clear part in the wordplay and reads as surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun stands for a person in general, as in looking after number one.

clue.text: Betweeen cat and bird, a weapon

indicators.note: the letter a is placed between the cat and the bird, so the three run side by side in that order

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a hawk is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A weapon is caught in the middle of a fight between a cat and a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomahawk is a light axe used by Native Americans as a tool and in battle.

clue.text: Tax people once in work for money received when unemployed

indicators.note: the tax people sit in the word for work

parts.note: a machine that works is said to go
IR is the Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority

explanation.surface: Former taxmen at work over the benefits paid to the jobless.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a giro was the cheque by which unemployment benefit was paid, hence the dole itself.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang names unemployment benefit after the bank transfer cheque used to pay it.

clue.text: Entering decline, custom to perform that's long and hairy

indicators.note: the custom and the performing word enter the word for decline

parts.note: to sag is to decline or droop
usage is custom or habit
to do something is to perform it

explanation.surface: A tradition in decline still gets a long, shaggy show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's long and hairy' is a jokey description of a dachshund, the long-bodied dog that comes in a long-haired variety.
explanation.definitionFit: The dachshund, nicknamed for its sausage shape, is a long dog and comes in a long-haired variety.

clue.text: Star exists in Altair, not half!

indicators.note: the word for exists goes in the shortened star name
only half of the six letters of Altair is kept, the first three

parts.note: something that exists is

explanation.surface: A star is to be found in Altair, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half!' is a British exclamation meaning 'and how!', which disguises the halving.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity of the first rank belongs to the top list of famous people.

clue.text: Malodorous gas, for the window!

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a pane is the glass of a window

explanation.surface: A stink of gas, so open the window!
explanation.definitionFit: This hydrocarbon is a fuel gas, given an added smell so leaks can be detected.

clue.text: Old film idol needs a licence to play an unknown

indicators.note: the letters are played with, set loose into a new order

parts.note: x is the unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: An ageing screen star needs a licence to perform as an unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1958 British war film is set in the desert, its hero longing for a cold beer in Alexandria.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a classic 1958 British war movie starring John Mills.

clue.text: Casually mention "vernal"is "green"

indicators.note: letters thrown together casually, in no fixed order, are rearranged

explanation.surface: Just mention in passing that 'vernal' means green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like a colour, but it is meant in its eco-friendly sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Green politics and policies are those concerned with protecting nature and the ecosystem.

clue.text: Career ruined snorting first of magic white powder

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the first of magic as if snorting it
a ruined career is wrecked, so its letters are rearranged
only the opening letter of magic is used

explanation.surface: A career is wrecked by snorting a magic white powder, cocaine by implication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges CAREER to CREAER, and 'snorting' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdered non-dairy whitener for coffee is sold under this name.

clue.text: Symbol of the United Nations about right, a fabulous thing

parts.note: UN is the standard abbreviation for the United Nations

indicators.note: the symbol goes about, around, the letter for right

parts.note: an icon is a symbol or emblem

explanation.surface: The UN's emblem turns out to be something from a fable.
explanation.definitionFit: This horned horse is a creature of fable and legend, fabulous in the old sense.

clue.text: European investigation under discussion

indicators.note: something under discussion is being spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a check is an inspection or investigation

explanation.surface: An inquiry into a European is being debated.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Czech Republic in central Europe.

clue.text: Old singers creep behind actors before overture to Idomeneo

indicators.note: the creep comes behind, after, the actors
the actors and creep come before the opening of the opera

parts.note: the cast of a play is its actors
a rat is a despicable person, a creep

indicators.note: the overture to a work is its opening, so the first letter

explanation.surface: An unpleasant type lurks behind the cast before the overture to Mozart's opera Idomeneo.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrated male sopranos were stars of baroque opera, a type of singer no longer made.

clue.text: Tall plant that's the same, a monster

parts.note: snap is the call in the card game when two matching cards appear
a dragon is a fire-breathing monster

explanation.surface: A tall plant that is just like a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: Snap is a children's card game where players call out on seeing two identical cards; the word also means identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Antirrhinum is a garden flower with tall spikes of blooms shaped like a mouth.

clue.text: Footballer in red?

parts.note: a player on one flank of a football team, and a red as in a communist, who sits on that side politically

explanation.surface: Which footballer plays in a red shirt?
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' looks like a team strip, but it means a socialist, someone on that wing of politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide attacking player on one side of the pitch, and also a radical socialist politician.

clue.text: March second following a quarter of the last month?

indicators.note: the second comes following, after, the month's opening
a quarter of the eight letters of the month is its first two

parts.note: December is the last month of the year
mo is short for moment, a second

explanation.surface: Was there a march just after the year's last quarter began?
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but is a protest march.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration is a protest march; this word is its short form.

clue.text: Drunk held wine as capital

indicators.note: drunk letters reel about, so they appear in a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk is holding wine as money, or so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the seat of government of India.

clue.text: Currently batting, openers in some trouble

parts.note: a cricketer at the crease batting is in

indicators.note: the openers in the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: The batsmen at the crease now, with the openers struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batter currently at the crease is 'in'. INST, short for instant, is old business English for 'of this month'.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation means in the present month, as in letters dated the 5th inst.

clue.text: Exert pressure on lover

definitions.meaning: a boyfriend or girlfriend, in informal speech

explanation.surface: Put the pressure on your partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to press tightly; the informal noun means a romantic partner.

clue.text: Device that makes chick peas choose Cheddar, perhaps?

definitions.text: Device that makes chick peas choose Cheddar, perhaps?

parts.words: Device that makes chick peas choose Cheddar, perhaps?
parts.note: swapping the opening sounds of chick peas gives pick cheese, which is choosing Cheddar; that swap is a verbal device named after an Oxford don

explanation.surface: What gadget makes chickpeas prefer Cheddar?
explanation.walkthrough: Exchanging the initial sounds turns 'chick peas' into 'pick cheese', and Cheddar is a cheese you might pick.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure of speech swapping initial sounds is named after the Reverend William Spooner.

clue.text: Dip tongue not very far at first?

indicators.note: the short distance comes at first, before the language

parts.note: 1 mm, one millimetre, is no distance at all
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: Dunk your tongue in, just a little at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of 1mm is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip something is to plunge it briefly into liquid.

clue.text: Affair's beginning, ennui initially concealed by a couple in trouble, accordingly going about it?

definitions.text: Affair's beginning, ennui initially concealed by a couple in trouble, accordingly going about it?

indicators.note: the beginning of Affair's is its first letter
the word for accordingly goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: duly means properly, accordingly

indicators.note: the first of ennui is concealed by, inside, two letters
a couple in trouble are its first two letters
only the initial letter of ennui is taken

explanation.surface: An affair begins with boredom, a couple in difficulty going about it as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed by' makes TER, the first of ennui inside the couple of letters; 'going about' wraps the word for accordingly round that. Read whole, the clue describes how an affair comes about.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital infidelity is an affair that starts from boredom in a troubled marriage.

clue.text: Obsession, fine and good

parts.note: a fine thread is thin

explanation.surface: An obsession can be fine and good.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something is to be fixated on it.

clue.text: Day after day, e's a brute

indicators.note: the weekday comes after the other letters

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday
the letter e is taken as written
Mon is short for Monday

explanation.surface: Day in, day out, E is a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend or devil is a cruel, savage creature.

clue.text: In Vietnam, I designed houses

indicators.note: the words house the answer, holding it inside them

explanation.surface: In Vietnam, I was the architect of the homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being among or in the middle of things is being in them.

clue.text: 5 to 9pm, say — say about 9 to 5 backwards!

indicators.note: the word for say goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

indicators.note: the numbers are written backwards, so read from right to left

parts.note: nine spelt out
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: From five to nine is the evening, so to speak, the office day reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns NINE V into VENIN, which 'about' puts inside EG. Nine to five is the standard office day.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours after work, from late afternoon to night, are an example of this time of day.

clue.text: A shocker ultimately within African country, a disease

indicators.note: the pieces go within the African country

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of shocker

explanation.surface: A shocking thing in an African country: a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: This mosquito-borne fever is an illness common in tropical countries.

clue.text: Transport operator needing fresh water source

indicators.note: a fresh version of the word is a new arrangement of its letters

parts.note: a river is a source of water

explanation.surface: A transport operator needs a supply of fresh water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' looks like it describes the water, but it rearranges NEEDING into ENGINED.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway worker who drives a locomotive operates a form of transport.
